correctness.rationale: Use independently sampled vertex probabilities with independent outgoing Bernoulli trials conditional on the probability at their common source. A path uses a different source for each edge, giving p^depth. An ancestor-descendant pair has joint indicator equal to the deeper indicator. For an incomparable pair, the only repeated source in the two paths is their lowest common ancestor, so the joint probability is E[Theta²] times p raised to the combined distinct-edge count minus two. This proves the baseline covariance formula and the variance excess after subtracting the deterministic-source case. Grouping pairs by lowest common ancestor gives the product of the two child-subtree sums for each child pair, multiplied by p to the ancestor depth. All terms are positive and at most 2, and there are at most binomial(n-1,2) pairs. No incomparable pair means an endpoint-rooted path; all nonroot pairs incomparable means a center-rooted star, where every exponent is zero. For convex order, condition on all other potential trials in the oriented tree. Reachability of the selected vertex does not depend on its outgoing trials, and its disjoint child subtrees have fixed nonnegative weights in the conditional count. The diagonal second derivative in the common Bernoulli parameter sums ordered mixed differences of the convex function over pairs of child activations, all nonnegative. Single-vertex replacements thus prove the order for the final count. The two-point abstract law attains the upper bound. The scope phrase about a supremum only in the finite-duration representation needs the qualification B>0: when B=0 the bound is attained by every law. At n=2 the whole count is 1 plus a Bernoulli(p) trial. Both supplied exact-rational scripts were read, not executed; the reported checks through n=6 corroborate finite cases, not the theorem for arbitrary size.
residual_risks: The theorem is about a single-root, disjoint-subtree model and an eventual count, not timings or cyclic graphs; extrema of B are not extrema of total variance across trees.

evidence: The October 25 prior statement also covers separate mean-preserving convex-order replacement for vertex-dependent laws. The October 13 record covers vertex probabilities in [0,1] and also supplies a sharp positive minimum among branching trees.

Wilkinson and Sharkey compare subset-hit probabilities up to time t; Vizi et al. compare pairwise-model reproduction quantities and derived final sizes; Hiraoka and Saramäki discuss matching tree marginals. None of those inspected literature statements is the full matching count result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The direct Resultary overlap is decisive. The literature comparisons distinguish different observables and are not used in place of same-count evidence.

evidence: For any closed-interval law of mean p, replace Theta by (1-epsilon)Theta+epsilon p. It lies in [0,1), still has mean p, and a common affine map preserves the input convex order. Every such law has a finite-duration representation in the earlier model.

The count probabilities on a finite tree are expectations of finite polynomials in the independent source probabilities. As epsilon tends to zero the probabilities, the stop-loss expectations and the variance therefore converge. The deterministic baseline formula itself follows from independent Bernoulli trials on the union of the two paths.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The closed-interval ordering and attainment follow directly by this continuity and the moment bound, and the earlier index formula already gives the variance excess there. The depth-sum spelling of the baseline and the postorder rearrangement of the same pair sum do not leave a distinct substantive remainder.

originality.rationale: The earlier Resultary finding 1d4b8a70bdd4 gives the same final-count convex order, mean, exact variance excess and weighted incomparable-pair index with the same path/star extrema. The endpoint-inclusive abstraction is the continuous closure of that result: the same mean and convex order can be preserved in the approximation. The n=2 addition is just one Bernoulli trial. The earlier record b769c52b1efb gives the variance formula directly even on the closed interval.
residual_risks: The 1993 source could contain further overlap, but this is neither established nor necessary for the failure based on the exact earlier findings.

value.rationale: For the abstract probability problem, the final-count convex order and exact variance sensitivity are meaningful observables. Here those same results are already present, including the sharp topology classification. Admitting a probability of one gives boundary attainment by a routine closure of the earlier model; n=2 and re-expressing the baseline do not constitute a separate finding of comparable scientific value.
residual_risks: This is a rejection of the duplicate and its minor extensions as a standalone contribution, not of the underlying mathematical question.
